Cautiously optimistic overall, consistent with the FOMC’s view that Q1 softness was transitory and with continued labor-market strength and inflation trending toward 2 percent. However, the Beige Book adds important nuance: reports across Districts indicate labor demand is constraining growth in manufacturing, transportation, and construction and is putting upward pressure on wages. Economic activity increased in several Districts and manufacturing continued to expand, but momentum is uneven—consumer spending varied by District and freight shipment growth slowed, signaling softer goods flow/logistics. On prices, input cost pressures are influencing selling prices, aligning with inflation near (but not markedly above) 2 percent.

Layering in SLOOS, financing conditions are mixed: tighter C&I terms at foreign banks and ongoing CRE concerns could modestly restrain business fixed investment despite firming, while consumer credit shows tighter auto standards but some easing in credit cards. Overall, gradual policy normalization remains appropriate, but conditions are not uniformly accommodative. This slightly tempers the positive signal relative to the initial read.
